question: Should OpenClaw adopt `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` as the public per-target-agent cap, with spawn admission honoring target, requester-session, and global limits?
rationale: Source inspection proves the capability gap, but the permanent configuration contract and composition semantics are product and API choices that automation should not set.

options.title: Add nested target cap
options.body: Add the setting under the existing per-agent `subagents` namespace and enforce it through shared native and ACP admission while retaining current safety caps.

options.title: Generalize named lanes
options.body: Introduce configurable spawn lanes and per-lane limits, accepting a broader model-facing and configuration surface.

options.title: Keep current limits
options.body: Decline the extra configuration surface and document that only global and requester-session concurrency controls are supported.

recommendation.title: Add nested target cap
recommendation.body: Add the setting under the existing per-agent `subagents` namespace and enforce it through shared native and ACP admission while retaining current safety caps.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history connects this person to the central concurrency resolver, lane application, and recent subagent policy work.
